sn56.38:1.1: “Bhikkhus, so long as the sun and moon have not arisen in the world, for just so long there is no manifestation of great light and radiance,
sn56.38:1.2: but then blinding darkness prevails, a dense mass of darkness;
sn56.38:1.3: for just so long day and night are not discerned, the month and fortnight are not discerned, the seasons and the year are not discerned.
sn56.38:2.1: “But, bhikkhus, when the sun and moon arise in the world, then there is the manifestation of great light and radiance;
sn56.38:2.2: then there is no blinding darkness, no dense mass of darkness;
sn56.38:2.3: then day and night are discerned, the month and fortnight are discerned, the seasons and year are discerned.
sn56.38:2.4: “So too, bhikkhus, so long as a Tathagata has not arisen in the world, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, for just so long there is no manifestation of great light and radiance,
sn56.38:2.5: but then blinding darkness prevails, a dense mass of darkness;
sn56.38:2.6: for just so long there is no explaining, teaching, proclaiming, establishing, disclosing, analysing, or elucidating of the Four Noble Truths.
sn56.38:3.1: “But, bhikkhus, when a Tathagata arises in the world, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One, then there is the manifestation of great light and radiance;
sn56.38:3.2: then no blinding darkness prevails, no dense mass of darkness;
sn56.38:3.3: then there is the explaining, teaching, proclaiming, establishing, disclosing, analysing, and elucidating of the Four Noble Truths.
sn56.38:3.5: The noble truth of suffering … the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
sn56.38:4.1: “Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is suffering.’… An exertion should be made to understand: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
